Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AdHocConversation

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AdHocConversation
public final class AdHocConversation extends Object
Where an agent's conversation lives, and how long it lives (CIB7-2137).

The agent meant is the one that drives the scope, and the turn runner says which call is that agent's (drive(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity, java.util.function.Supplier<T>)). Any other AI agent task inside an ad hoc sub process, in a plain one or used as a tool of an agentic one, keeps its conversation where every AI agent task keeps it: at the process level, so a later task with the same memoryId continues it after the scope has ended (CIB7-2232).

perEntry, the default and what the loop always did, keeps it on the agent state: the conversation belongs to the scope execution, so entering the scope again starts a new one. perActivity keeps it on a holder one level up, so every entry of this scope within the enclosing scope continues the same conversation — what a feedback loop needs, where the process leaves the scope for a user task and comes back.

The holder is an event-scope execution with activity = null under the execution enclosing the scope, the same trick AdHocAgentState uses one level down, and for the same reason: it is a sibling of the scope rather than an ancestor of its tools, so a tool writing the memory's name creates its own variable at the process instance instead of rewriting the conversation. It is removed with the enclosing scope, and clearing its activity keeps it out of Cockpit's activity tree. A holder directly under the process instance survives until that instance ends and blocks all migration while it exists. This MVP restriction awaits the generic engine SPI in CIB7-2167; the engine must not depend on AI-specific state.

Only the configured message window survives, not all history. With perActivity, an unspecified chatMemoryMaxMessages defaults to at least 53 messages and grows with the effective model-call limit. The minimum is 2 * maxModelCalls + 3; it is a bounded window, not a guarantee of unlimited history or of retaining arbitrary tool-call batches. An explicitly smaller window is rejected. perEntry keeps the connector's existing 20-message default and behaviour. Sequential multi-instance iterations share this holder and total cap: later iterations are re-entries and use followUp on their first turn.

Recognised by the activity id it carries, not by a fixed marker: two agentic scopes under one enclosing execution each have a holder, and AdHocAgentState.find(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.pvm.delegate.ActivityExecution) — which matches a fixed marker — would hand out whichever came first.

    • isPerActivity

      public static boolean isPerActivity(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      Whether this scope keeps its conversation across entries.

      An unknown value reads as PER_ENTRY rather than failing, the same direction positiveProperty falls back in: the parse listener already refused it at deployment, so a value arriving here at all means a model that predates that rule, and the old behaviour is the safe one.

    • enclosing

      protected static PvmExecutionImpl enclosing(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      The nearest enclosing scope execution — the process instance for a scope modelled directly in the process, the enclosing sub process otherwise.

      getParentScopeExecution rather than getParent(): behind a parallel gateway the direct parent is a concurrent execution the engine compacts away when the branches join, and the conversation has to outlive that.

      public static void enterScope(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      Counts this entry of the scope, so a later turn can tell a re-entry from a first entry.

      Called when the scope is entered, in that transaction, like the agent state itself: the first turn runs in a job of its own and must already see the right count.

    • outsideDrive

      public static <T> T outsideDrive(Supplier<T> call)
      Runs call, a tool the driving agent called, outside the agent's call. The tools of an agentic step run within drive(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity, java.util.function.Supplier<T>), on the same thread, and so does everything the engine does while they run: a tool's BPMN error, caught by a boundary event on the scope, cancels the scope there and then, and the scope's end listeners run on the very execution drive(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity, java.util.function.Supplier<T>) marks. They would pass for the driving agent and could read or clear its conversation, which neither a tool nor code on the scope may (CIB7-2232). The mark is put back afterwards, for the agent's own writes once the tool has run.

    • drivenScope

      public static ExecutionEntity drivenScope(ExecutionEntity execution)
      execution, while drive(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity, java.util.function.Supplier<T>) runs for it on this thread: the conversation read or written on it is then the scope's own. null for every other execution, that of an AI agent task inside the scope included.

    • memoryId

      public static String memoryId(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      What names the conversation.

      perEntry: the scope execution, so every entry is its own. perActivity: the enclosing execution and the activity id, both of which the next entry of the same scope finds again. Derived rather than read off the holder, so it stays a pure function and a read path never has to create one.

    • turnsTotal

    • beginTurnTotal

      public static int beginTurnTotal(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution, String turnId)
      Counts the turn turnId against every entry together, once, and returns the count.

      Zero without a holder, which is every perEntry scope: there is no total to count, and the caller's > 0 guard on the configured limit never fires.
